title: Sideframe LensFlow and Session-Persisted Switcher
creator: Amara Venkataraman
description: Redesign the console left rail and workspace switch behavior to introduce a compact sideframe ('Sideframe') that surfaces contextual 'lens' views (cost, rollouts, traces) and a session-persisted workspace switcher so engineers can maintain task context across navigation and refreshes.
background: Current console navigation forces users to fully change context when switching workspaces or drilling into per-model dashboards. Customers building multi-tenant UIs and SREs running rollouts repeatedly lose their selection state; billing owners struggle to keep cost lenses visible while exploring traces. This makes troubleshooting, rollout analysis, and cost investigation more frictioned than necessary.
goals: Provide a compact, always-available contextual pane (Sideframe) that slides from the left and can pin cost/rollout/traces lenses
Make workspace switching session-persisted (store in user session/local storage + server-side fallback) so selected workspace, pinned lenses, and route breadcrumbs survive reloads
Improve discoverability of rollouts and cost-impact lanes without increasing cognitive load or taking primary screen real estate
Ensure accessibility (keyboard nav, screen reader labels) and responsive behavior on small viewports
non_goals: Complete nav rebrand — this is an incremental IA change focused on context surfaces
Changing global perms or RBAC rules — security or role changes handled in separate ticket
Replacing existing dashboards — we surface them via lenses; content stays in current dashboards
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to open a rollout lens while keeping my current dashboard so I can compare before/after metrics without losing filters
As a billing engineer, I want to pin the cost lens across workspaces so I can track spend while exploring models
As a PM, I want workspace switcher state preserved after a browser crash so my session resumes where I left off
As an engineer with keyboard-only workflows, I want to open the Sideframe and cycle lenses without using the pointer
acceptance_criteria: Sideframe opens from left with keyboard shortcut (G then L) and via a slim affordance on the left rail
Lenses: cost, rollouts, traces available as top-level cards inside Sideframe; each lens links to canonical dashboard and supports lightweight inline interactions (short filters, time range adjust)
Workspace switcher persists selection to sessionStorage and server-side user preference endpoint; switching back restores pinned lenses and Sideframe open state
Sideframe pins collapse into rail icons at narrow breakpoints and maintain accessible labels
Performance: initial Sideframe open animation <= 150ms and initial lens payloads lazy-loaded with placeholder skeletons
QA: keyboard tabbable order verified and aria labels present for all interactive elements
deliverables: Figma prototype (desktop + tablet) showing Sideframe open/closed states, pin/unpin flow, and workspace persistence
Confluence PRD detailing IA, telemetry events, and rollout plan
Design tokens and CSS spec for Sideframe (width, motion, z-index)
Handoff package: component specs, interaction notes, edge-case flows
design_decisions: Use a left-side slide-over (instead of overlay modal) to keep main content context visible
Session persistence implemented via sessionStorage with server-side user preference write-back on explicit pin action
Pinning is a user action (soft pin in session vs hard pin to account preferences) — default is soft session pin
Lenses are lazy-loaded; cost lens precomputes a light summary (3 metrics) server-side to show instant value
On small screens the Sideframe compresses to a vertical icon strip and becomes a modal only for deep lens interactions
tradeoffs: Pros: faster context switching, lower cognitive cost, better cross-dashboard comparisons
Cons: added complexity for legacy routes; requires coordination with routing team and telemetry to avoid duplicate events
We avoid automatic hard saving of pins to respect users who prefer ephemeral sessions; this sacrifices convenience for privacy/control
next_steps: Collect feedback from PM and Eng in the design review (scheduled 2025-02-18)
Iterate prototype to include rollout variants: canary vs phased and explicit traffic sliders
Finalize telemetry contract with Eng: events.sideframe.open, events.lens.pin, events.workspace.persist
Create engineering tickets for Sideframe component, lens adapters, session API endpoint
UX research: 5 moderated sessions to validate discoverability and pin mental models
reviews: PM review (Nina Ortiz): wants clearer affordance for 'pin to account' vs 'pin to session' — asked for a tooltip and confirmation for hard pin
Eng review (Sahil Mehta): raised concerns about duplicate route events and proposed debounce logic; advised API design for lightweight lens payloads
Security review (Anika Zhou): asked that session persistence not leak workspace IDs in public logs; recommended encryption of server-side preferences
Design critique (internal): suggested stronger microcopy for the Sideframe close action and focus trap behavior improvements
